claims.author: apoelstra
claims.harm: a raw codex32 seed allows an attacker to sweep funds without needing the wallet passphrase
claims.quote: the seed is the seed -- once an attacker has it, it's game over. He doesn't need the passphrase or any other part of the wallet to sweep coins

settled_by.quote: Yes, you're right. I thought the passphrase deterministically modified the seed to create the BIP 32 Extended Key, but that's not the case.

claims.author: Sjors
claims.harm: backing up raw keys in custom seed RPCs bypasses descriptor backups needed for complex wallets and fragments key import logic away from addhdkey
claims.quote: It seems to me that codex32 only plays a role in (1). And so importing it should be done with `addhdkey`. Exporting could be done with `gethdkeys`.

claims.author: BenWestgate
claims.harm: restoring solely from seed lacks wallet birth timestamps needed for efficient rescanning and lacks descriptor associations
claims.quote: we need the timestamp no? Other approaches made the import/restore command require a corresponding descriptor to function and that seems more robust for existing wallets.

notes: Initial record for the POC PR. Reviewers support the concept of paper backups in principle, but open objections remain regarding the architecture: Sjors and BenWestgate noted that seed recovery without descriptors and birth timestamps is incomplete for modern descriptor wallets, and Sjors prefers integration via addhdkey.

participants.note: pointed out that codex32 seeds are unencrypted and bypass wallet passphrases
argued key material import/export should use addhdkey/gethdkeys and must account for descriptors
pointed out missing timestamps for rescans and urged support for share sets and descriptors
Concept ACK for introducing paper-based wallet backups

support.author: rkrux
support.reason: paper-based backups are a ubiquitous industry standard and timely now that legacy wallets are removed
